- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out extremes using 7-day moving average of history.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from neutral to positive, model often fails to adjust; delay forecast adjustment until next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is low and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
